Phylogeny
¨Tracing Phylogeny
¤Behavioral Traits
  nParental care, mating calls, etc.
¤Molecular Traits
  nSystematics assumes:
  nTwo species with similar base-pair sequences are assumed to be closely related
  nTwo species with differing base-pair sequences are assumed to be only distantly related
explanation: To trace phylogeny, systematists analyze behavioral and molecular traits. Behavioral traits include actions like parental care behaviors and species-specific mating calls. Molecular traits are particularly powerful: systematics operates on the assumption that species sharing highly similar DNA base-pair sequences are closely related (sharing a recent common ancestor), whereas species with highly divergent base-pair sequences are only distantly related (sharing a more ancient common ancestor).

questions.q: What assumption does systematics make when comparing the DNA base-pair sequences of two species?
opts: Species with similar base-pair sequences are assumed to be closely related.
Species with similar base-pair sequences are assumed to be distantly related.
DNA sequence similarity is completely unrelated to evolutionary history.
Prokaryotes do not have base-pair sequences.
questions.exp: Systematics assumes that a higher similarity in DNA base-pair sequences reflects a closer evolutionary relationship and recent common ancestry.
